races.title: State Senate, District 50
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kevin Corbin
cands.bio: Republican state senator for North Carolina District 50 since 2021. Insurance agency owner from Franklin (The Corbin Agency, Blue Ridge Insurance Group). Served in the NC House (District 120) 2017–2021, on the Macon County board of commissioners 2011–2016, and 20 years on the Macon County School Board.
cands.gaps: The pages available did not show any documented action or statement by Corbin on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing pay or penalties, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. No documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements were found. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate surveys, so there are no self-reported positions. His exact birth year is uncertain (1960 or 1961), and the pages do not say where he grew up beyond his Franklin High School graduation. Wikipedia notes he supports Medicaid expansion and a bill extending postpartum coverage to 12 months, but that does not bear on the listed topics.

cands.name: Tom Downing
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina State Senate District 50 in 2026. He advanced without a primary and lost the general election to incumbent Kevin Corbin (R). The sources provided give no information on his occupation or past offices.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from three Sway voting groups: Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress (Vote for Peace), Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy (Tevin Davis), and Waves of Democracy (Terri Robinson).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Tom Downing was born or raised, when he moved to North Carolina, or his occupation and work history. We found no record of prior elected office. We found no documented actions in office, and no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or teacher pay. The only source was his Ballotpedia page, including his survey answers. No news coverage or controversies turned up.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he said North Carolina is ranked 50th of 50 states for public school funding and that it must increase. He asked whether the Republican majority is trying to ruin public schools in order to privatize them.

back-police-order.evidence: In his Ballotpedia survey he listed increased public safety pay and benefits among the areas where the General Assembly needs to act.
